prerequisites: Fundamentals of computer science and practical experience in imperative programming (e.g., in the C programming language)

learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to apply the concepts of Object-Oriented Programming in C++.
Students can object-orientedly model simple data processing tasks and implement them practically with the class concept of the C++ programming language.
Students can efficiently and modularly structure extensive and complex programs through inheritance.
Students can apply exception handling in C++ to robustly and efficiently catch errors.
Students are able to clearly structure program code across multiple files and by using namespaces.
Students can evaluate and classify algorithms and programs with regard to time efficiency.

Students learn fundamental algorithms for search methods, sorting methods, and data storage (lists) and can program them object-orientedly in the C++ programming language and evaluate their time efficiency.
Students receive a general introduction to the topic of sustainability in the context of algorithm time efficiency.

syllabus_topics: Concepts of object-oriented programming (classes, data encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism)
Object-oriented programming in the C++ programming language
Non-object-oriented elements of the C++ programming language (exception handling, data streams, namespaces, functions with default parameters)
"Sustainable Computing" and time efficiency of algorithms
Algorithms and data structures: search methods, sorting algorithms, data containers (lists, stacks, queues)
Introduction and discussion of the UN's sustainability goals (SDGs)
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination and proof of performance. The grade's relevance for the final grade is determined according to the study and examination regulations (SPO).
